## Verdict
SECURITY NO-BLOCKER for the current e04s01-local-conversation-transport working-tree candidate, round2/max5. No actionable vulnerability survived the required confidence ≥8/10 threshold. Findings: 0. This is a specialist security conclusion, not a general 32-item quality score, story acceptance, complete ACP acceptance, or authorization for publication/live-provider activity.

## Method and scope
Read the full review brief including the post-suspend addendum, CONVENTIONS, threat model, approved PLAN, ADR0004, integration contract, S01 story/tasks and test-plan rows. Reviewed current files directly rather than assuming HEAD contains the integrated candidate. Examined production controls, adjacent lifecycle/provenance code, fixture behavior, test assertions, documentation and supplied runtime evidence. No files were changed. No commands, builds, tests, linters, formatters, payloads, runtime probes, provider/auth operations or network requests were executed by this reviewer. No other security/general review report was consulted.

## Security traces and controls
1. Authority and atomic admission: daemon.rs:433–455 resolves the submitted target's control capability, obtains the server-authorized controller identity and prepares the original immutable action. control.rs:1194–1214 rechecks live owner/reference/generation under the target mutex and invokes the broker commit before releasing that mutex. acp.rs:484–654 independently checks the captured generation, exact target tuple, lifecycle, duplicate-call tombstone, capacity and foreground state before canonical publication. Revocation/force/cancel use that same target ordering point. Accepted writer records do not perform a subsequent owner lookup or rebind to a new grant.
2. Routes and provenance: daemon.rs:1236–1260 rejects native operations addressed to ACP and terminal-shaped ACP selectors. control.rs:1280 onward rejects ACP native forwarding independently. tui.rs:988–1025 consumes active-ACP events even when the editor returns no action; the double-prefix path separately avoids native forwarding. NativeControl::input also rejects known ACP targets. The editor captures target/control/generation at first edit, clears mismatched drafts and returns complete envelopes unchanged. Server connection identity reaches admit_acp from dispatch/serve, not a request field. View/consent/activity controls require the original live attachment connection; views-backgrounded compares actual target kind and ID. Borrowed control does not create human provenance.
3. Exact identities and RPC lifetime: Target deserialization is closed and requires explicit session_id, including bootstrap null. Exact target/instance/connection/session equality is checked against canonical state. Call IDs remain tombstoned across completed-work eviction and owner changes, with a final close slot reserved. Outgoing RPC records are inserted before writer visibility. The single application consumer handles bootstrap/auth/prompt replies and updates without synchronous result waits. Responses require an exact retained RPC ID; update session IDs must match. Agent updates are not assigned to the latest prompt by arrival. Caller loss does not delete broker work. Force and ordinary pending cancellation do not send protocol cancel or terminate the process; keep/withdraw preserve the human owner. Explicit interruption targets the exact foreground prompt, and only the original prompt's cancelled result confirms cancellation.
4. Unsupported delegation: S01 does not advertise form, filesystem or terminal capabilities. Incoming unsupported requests receive exact-ID protocol errors; elicitation receives invalid-params. Advertised agent-type authentication requires an explicit authorized action; client/terminal/unknown method types cannot be selected. There is no URL opening, filesystem delegation, credential collection or automatic approval path. Late permission handling while explicitly cancelling produces Cancelled, not an invented allow/deny selection.
5. Capacity and ordered failure: acp.rs:1026–1088 checks the 1 MiB frame limit before accumulation, including newline-free/partial input. Reader reservation and consumer-owned in-flight frames remain charged against ingress count/bytes. Egress accounting retains dequeued writer-owned frames until completion. RPC, prompt, argv, IDs, call tombstones, transcript/completed history, stderr and global live/reserved target limits are bounded. Response-capacity failure fails the instance rather than dropping a responder and claiming continuity. Stderr continues draining after retention fills. Ordered EOF/failure processes preceding complete frames and marks unresolved work unknown; late write evidence does not overwrite an already-observed protocol outcome. History eviction exposes gaps without evicting live RPC mappings. Unknown process-identity/cleanup outcomes remain retained, incomplete and capacity-charged.
6. Lifecycle, process ownership and locks: open reserves broker capacity, publishes target/initial authority and starts asynchronously; lifetime.with_live prevents late bootstrap publication after target end. Close/shutdown end authority and broker state together, with cleanup outside those locks. The owned worker uses setsid, direct argv spawn, pre-publication ProcessTree capture and the existing birth-qualified freeze/rescan termination primitive. The uncaptured fallback signals only the still-unreaped owned group before wait, not a reused post-reap group. Cleanup joiners serialize outside admission. Snapshot copies topology descriptors before ACP/ownership projections; event drainage releases component locks before topology publication. No reachable new authority↔ACP/topology lock cycle, or pipe/process wait under authority/ACP state, was found in the inspected paths.
7. Privacy and inert rendering: public ACP projections expose bounded identities/dispositions and numeric protocol error codes, not prompt bodies, raw provider errors, command/env, stderr or arbitrary agent identity content. Content inspection is explicit and incremental. Direct executable/argv launch performs no shell interpolation. Broker and editor sanitize controls; editor JSON formatting is bounded and rendered as Ratatui text, not host escape instructions. No new reachable command/terminal injection or credential disclosure path was established.

## Post-suspend repairs
Reviewed observe/draw_panel/panel_event/after_draw together with the actual top-level draw/event ordering. Changed force facts invalidate eligibility; new panels, resize, scrolling and clipping still invalidate it. First presentation becomes confirmable only after a successful full draw and drained input. An unchanged fully-visible repaint may preserve a completed presentation. Enter still checks the captured observation, and the server compare rejects a concurrent owner/reservation change. Reviewed the original native test's queued-before-draw, clipped viewport, changed-owner, no-replay and same-process assertions. ShellReportGate now clears inherited accepted-socket nonblocking mode before framed callback reads; its delayed original-request, exact-target settlement and replacement-target non-effect assertions remain substantive. Neither repair establishes a new authority bypass.

## Six S01 scenario assessments
- SC-e04s01-P0-01: reviewed separate-view reservation, one owned connection/session, canonical prompt/stream and actual same-session API42/human57 CLI/PTY evidence. No fake terminal or security blocker found.
- SC-e04s01-P0-02: reviewed closed mutation shapes, control/target/generation/call validation, busy foreground semantics and negative-effect test assertions. No reachable stale-input admission bypass found.
- SC-e04s01-P0-03: reviewed asynchronous bootstrap/auth, retained exact RPCs, unsupported responders, caller disconnect, prompt-error foreground release and explicit authentication. No implicit authentication, cancellation, steering or identity substitution found.
- SC-e04s01-P0-04: reviewed frame, ingress, egress, in-flight/reserved and history accounting plus hostile real-peer fixtures and failure/responsiveness assertions. No confidence≥8 resource-boundary vulnerability found.
- SC-e04s01-P0-05: reviewed startup/close/shutdown publication races, capture-failure accounting, owned descendant/sentinel assertions and native-shell retirement isolation. No new unrelated-process signalling or closed-target resurrection path established.
- SC-e04s01-P1-06: reviewed metadata/content separation, synthetic privacy assertions, incremental gap handling and capped continued stderr drainage. No new content/credential leak or executable rendering path established.
These assessments combine static reasoning with reviewed evidence; none is an independently rerun acceptance verdict.

## Verification evidence reviewed
artifact://1036 includes the original native force regression passing, current seven ACP library tests, twenty S01 integration tests, thirty-four native ownership cases and twenty-three nonignored legacy agent cases, plus successful workspace regression/check/build/Clippy output. Reviewed the supplied ledger reporting workspace335/30 suites/10 ignored, formatting, Bun8/49 assertions and Zsh syntax; Bun/Zsh were not independently executed or their separate raw logs independently inspected. The current e04s01-resume-cli-pty-smoke.json records one session, API42/human57, paste local until Enter, revoked draft not replayed, observer no work, approved settlement_boundary retained-work panel, deliberate visible human force, preserved native IDs, restored termios, peer absent before fallback, TUI/host/daemon exit0 and joined bounded outer drainer. Capture-failure invariant tests and actual uncaptured-group cleanup test are distinct: they do not prove an induced OS metadata outage. Retained failure/diagnosis records were treated as limitations/history, not substituted for current proof.

## False-positive exclusions and limits
Explicit same-user local executable selection, inherited adapter credentials and agent-owned tools are trust boundaries, not a sandbox or privilege-escalation finding. Existing accepted e03 native application-fence defects and historical review caps remain unchanged. Later S02 forms/permissions and S03/S04 acceptance were not treated as missing S01 functionality. Explicit unknown cleanup reservation is conservative failure accounting, not successful cleanup. Public opaque IDs and deliberate local content reads are not, by themselves, unauthorized secret access. Resource exhaustion was reviewed because this assignment expressly includes CWE-400; it was not dismissed by generic security-skill exclusions.

This was a static review with supplied local deterministic-peer runtime evidence, not exploit execution, independent verification, dependency vulnerability scanning, real-adapter compatibility proof, OS process-metadata fault injection, or proof against malicious same-user process escape. No provider/model/auth/global/default actions occurred. No new confidence≥8 security blocker remains within the assigned scope.

deferred.reason: Independent execution and live compatibility were explicitly prohibited. Reviewed existing local deterministic-peer/CLI/PTY evidence only; no claim of independently rerun checks, real-provider compatibility or induced OS metadata outage.

Explicit scope exclusions: unchanged accepted e03 native-fence defects, same-user launch/agent-tool trust boundary, and later S02–S04 acceptance. No security finding was suppressed merely because it involved resource consumption.
